documents: Published paper (PDF): Li, Liu, Fang & Tang (2022), International Journal of Climatology 42(13), 6996-7012

entry.evidence: the skill of RCMs in simulating the wind speed still needs further investigation

steps.action: The authors pose two aims: evaluate how well RCMs reproduce the spatiotemporal pattern and extremes of inland and offshore 10-m wind over China, and test how resolution, physics schemes and spectral nudging affect the simulations.
steps.quote: The purpose of this study is to (a) evaluate the RCMs' performances in reproducing the spatiotemporal characteristics and the extremity

steps.action: They design 14 configurations of WRF and RegCM4 across CORDEX-EA-I (50 km) and EA-II (25 km), varying the radiation scheme (CAM, RRTMG), the land surface model (NOAH, CLM4, BATS, CLM3) and spectral nudging (on or off, nudged variables, coefficient, wavenumber 3 or 6), and define five inland subregions and an offshore region.
steps.quote: SN technique is applied in some of WRF experiments with different nudging parameters including nudged variables and nudging coefficients

steps.action: They run the RCM hindcasts driven by ERA-Interim for 1989-2008 and output 10-m wind speed.
steps.quote: The two RCMs are driven by the ERA-Interim reanalysis data from European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)

steps.action: They assemble the reference data: CMA daily wind at more than 2000 stations and ERA5 for inland China, CCMP satellite-based analysis and ERA5 offshore. The reliability of ERA5 and CCMP is cited from other studies, and simulations are interpolated to the stations or to the CCMP grid.
steps.quote: One is daily mean wind speed dataset at more than 2000 meteorological stations with anemometers at 10-m height above the ground

steps.action: They compare the 20-year mean inland wind patterns with stations using SCC and RMSE (Figures 2, 3): patterns are reproduced, but every RCM overestimates wind speed.
steps.quote: all RCMs significantly overestimate the near-surface wind speed over most areas in China

steps.action: They contrast configurations for inland skill. Higher resolution (WNC-II vs WNC-I) improves skill and radiation scheme has little effect. SN reduces biases and nudging parameters in EA-I matter little, while wavenumber 6 beats 3 in EA-II. Skill is sensitive to the land surface model (CLM3 beats BATS in RegCM4).
steps.quote: WRF can improve the simulation of surface wind speed with the increase of horizontal resolution

steps.action: They compare the offshore mean wind patterns with CCMP (Figure 4): all RCMs reach SCC above 0.7, and ERA5 agrees closely with CCMP.
steps.quote: all the RCMs reproduce the spatial distributions of offshore wind speed with the SCCs above 0.7

steps.action: They repeat the configuration contrasts offshore: resolution gives a slight improvement, SN corrects overestimation, and the land surface model has an obvious impact.
steps.quote: the added value of spectral nudging technique can also be found over offshore China

steps.action: They compare temporal variation: seasonal cycles (Figure 5), monthly TCC and RMSE maps (Figures 6, 7) and interannual SCC and RMSE series (Figure 8). Simulated inland peaks come a month early and biases are larger in winter than in summer.
steps.quote: The biases between the simulations and observation in winter are larger than in summer.

steps.action: They test whether the configuration effects hold for temporal metrics, across five subregions, offshore, and from year to year, with ERA5-against-station agreement as a baseline: resolution, SN and land surface model effects recur.
steps.quote: Similar conclusions can also be drawn over five subregions in China.

steps.action: They compare the 95th-percentile (extreme) wind with stations and CCMP (Figures 9, 10): the Inner Mongolia maximum is reproduced, but overestimation reaches up to 4 m/s over southeast China.
steps.quote: significant overestimations can be found over most areas of inland China

steps.action: They contrast configurations for extremes: higher resolution and SN improve skill, radiation scheme has little effect, CLM3 beats BATS, and WNCS6-II reaches RMSE below 1.5 m/s offshore.
steps.quote: the spectral nudging technique has great impact on the performances of both WRF CORDEX-EA-I and CORDEX-EA-II simulations

steps.action: They propose two candidate causes of the overestimation: biased low-level circulation (850 hPa wind) and land-sea surface temperature contrast. Only CORDEX-EA-II runs are analysed, with ERA5 as reference.
steps.quote: Due to the fact that low level circulation and surface heat distribution can directly influence the near-surface wind speed

steps.action: They compare 850 hPa wind with ERA-Interim and ERA5 (Figure 11): the driver's high bias is inherited by non-nudged runs and reduced by SN. They compare 2-m temperature biases with ERA5 (Figure 12): a winter cold bias over land increases the land-sea gradient, and a reduced summer gradient explains RCC-II's good summer wind.
steps.quote: the wind speed from ERA-Interim is larger than that from ERA5

steps.action: They keep the conclusions: RCMs reproduce wind patterns with systematic overestimation, finer resolution, SN and suitable physics improve skill, and inherited 850 hPa wind and land-sea temperature gradient biases partly explain the overestimation.
steps.quote: It is concluded that finer spatial resolution, preciser boundary conditions and more appropriate physical processes can improve the RCMs' skill.

tree.answer: Systematic overestimation of near-surface wind by RCMs over China; model skill is the phenomenon
Yes, wind is observed directly by station anemometers and by a satellite-based analysis (CCMP)
Evaluate RCM skill and its sensitivity to resolution, physics schemes and spectral nudging
For the bias cause: 850 hPa wind inherited from ERA-Interim versus land-sea temperature gradient; the two are treated as complementary, not rival
No distinct predictions stated for the candidate causes
Conditions set in model configurations (resolution, schemes, nudging)
Effects recur across two reference datasets, five subregions, offshore, temporal metrics and extremes
Kept: resolution and SN improve skill, and the overestimation is partly explained

end.claim: WRF and RegCM4 CORDEX-EA simulations reproduce the spatial and seasonal patterns of inland and offshore wind over China but overestimate speed, especially inland; finer resolution, spectral nudging and a suitable land surface model reduce the biases.

decisive_move.sentence: The comparison of the 14 configurations against station and CCMP references by SCC and RMSE (Figure 3 and its successors) produces both the skill characterization and the configuration effects.

gates.evidence: The experiments were designed to investigate the impact of configurations, not to test a stated hypothesis (p. 6998). Skill comparisons could have shown no improvement from resolution or SN, but no significance tests or preset thresholds are used. The bias-cause analysis is post hoc on CORDEX-EA-II runs only (p. 7009), and nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Spatial and temporal correlation coefficients and RMSE as skill metrics
High-performance computing enabling 25 km CORDEX-EA-II runs

limits: Each configuration is a single run. Inference: internal variability is not assessed, and no significance tests separate configuration effects from noise. The configuration set is not fully crossed: resolution is compared only for some CAM/NOAH settings, and RegCM4 has no SN runs, so attributions to individual factors are partly confounded. Sub-claim at a different status: the 850 hPa wind and land-sea temperature gradient mechanisms are best_explanation, supported by co-located biases rather than a targeted experiment. Ocean temperature is prescribed from ERA-Interim, and the discussion uses ERA5, a reanalysis from the same centre, as reference. Inference: the reference is not independent of the driver's family. Minor inconsistencies appear: 'WNCS63-II' (p. 7009), and the Figure 12 caption says 1989-2009 while the text says 1989-2008. composition none_fits because this is a model-evaluation and sensitivity study: conditions are set in simulations and there are no rival hypotheses with a crucial test, no trace series and no prior capability characterization step.
